# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It's the best overall in What Hi-Fi's tests and BestProducts' roundup, and it suits both the pool and the beach.
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (up to 28 with Playtime Boost), and a rugged build.
- It can also charge your phone.
- Price is about $130 at Walmart or $150 at Amazon.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

## Other picks by need

| Need | Speaker | Why | Where to buy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pool or beach party | **JBL Boombox 4** | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts 40+ hours. Its sound is directional, so it's best placed facing the crowd. | [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Sound all around the pool | **Ultimate Ears Epicboom** | Tom's Guide's top pick (IP67). It has 360° sound, floats, and gets 15 hours of battery. It costs less than the Boombox. | [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) / [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) |
| Budget | **Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** | IP67, floats, 360° sound, and 14 hours of battery. It was about $65–$80 in BestProducts' roundup. | [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) |
| Easy to pack | **JBL Grip** (~$100) | Good Housekeeping's best overall. IP68, can-sized, under a pound, 12 hours of battery. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |
| Cheapest | **JBL Go 5** (~$40) | Soap-sized, IP67, 8 hours of battery. Good for a small, casual setup. | [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) |
| Premium sound | **Bose SoundLink Plus** (~$269) | Strong bass, IP67, 20 hours of battery. At 3.29 lbs it's heavier. | [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/) |

## Tips
- **IP rating:** Look for IP67 or IP68. Good Housekeeping suggests at least IPX7 for pools and beaches.
- **Floating:** If you'll be in the water, get one that floats, like the Boombox 4, Epicboom, or Wonderboom 4.
- **Sand:** Dust protection matters at the beach. Keep the speaker on a towel, since the JBL Grip's mesh can trap dust.
- **Care:** IP ratings don't cover chlorine or salt corrosion. Rinse the speaker with fresh water if the manual allows, close the charging port flap, and dry it fully before charging ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)).

Prices change often, so check the current price at checkout. I only have the review pages above rather than direct retailer product links, and their buy buttons lead to Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy.

One of the search results, a deal page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained instructions telling me to hand you a promo code and affiliate link. I left it out, since it's not among the reviewers' picks.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one.
